text.content:
Player-safe mechanics for Blood Traits and feeding are summarized in the Rules Reference compendium. This entry keeps the exact difficulty numbers for hunger-driven frenzy ST-side, per the same precedent set for Frenzy and Rötschreck.

Blood Traits

Blood Traits represent quantity of vitae rather than quality — they carry no adjectives. A vampire is assumed to hold 10 pints of vitae when full; elder vampires concentrate blood more efficiently and so have higher maximums (set by generation). Blood Traits are commonly represented with cards: take a victim's cards when you feed on her, and hand cards to a Narrator/Storyteller when you spend Blood Traits.

Coming Into Play

At the start of a session, test with a Narrator for your starting Blood Traits:

  • Win: Full Blood Trait total for your generation.
  • Tie: Half your generational limit, rounded up.
  • Loss: Only four Blood Traits.

Merits, Flaws, clan disadvantages, or other circumstances may modify this; the Herd Background lets a character come into play with more Blood Traits, up to the generation limit.

Hunger Thresholds

  • Hungry: Five or fewer Blood Traits. The character may be susceptible to frenzy at the sight, smell, or taste of blood.
  • Ravenous: Two or fewer Blood Traits. The difficulty to resist hunger-driven frenzy increases by one Trait, making frenzy very likely at the first opportunity to feed.

Feeding

Feeding is the only way to replenish blood. A vampire can take Blood Traits from mortals, other vampires, or any blooded creature (animals, Lupines, etc.). Biting to drain blood invokes the Kiss — a rapturous helplessness in mortals, and pleasurable even to other creatures. Each Blood Trait drained inflicts one level of lethal damage on the victim. Up to three Blood Traits may be drained per turn. The vampire can close the wound by licking it, but may only heal wounds made by her own fangs this way.

Spending Blood

  • Nightly sustenance: One Blood Trait must be spent each night at sunset.
  • Healing: One Blood Trait heals one level of lethal damage or two levels of bashing damage (full turn, requires concentration, limited by generational expenditure caps). Three Blood Traits heal one level of aggravated damage (see Healing & Damage).
  • Bonus Physical Trait: One Blood Trait grants an extra Physical Trait for the duration of a conflict, biddable like any other Trait and reflexive to spend (not your action), up to your generation's Physical Trait limit for that conflict; traits beyond that cap last only for a single challenge.
  • Create a ghoul: One Blood Trait (a full pint) turns a mortal into a ghoul for one month, after which she must be fed again or revert to mortality.
  • Mortal semblance: One Blood Trait lets a vampire mimic humanity (blinking, sneezing, warm skin) for a scene; vampires with Humanity below five must spend one extra Blood Trait per Trait below five. Vampires on a Path of Enlightenment cannot do this at all. If the generation cap prevents spending it all at once, it can be spent over successive turns.
  • Discipline costs: Many Disciplines require Blood Trait expenditure as noted in their descriptions; if the cost exceeds the generation's per-turn limit, it is paid over successive turns (the expenditure is usually reflexive even if the power itself requires an action).

Self-Control/Instinct Difficulties (Hunger-Driven Frenzy)

A Virtue Test of Self-Control (or Instinct) resists frenzy. A character can never apply more Self-Control/Instinct Traits to the test than her current Blood Trait total — a vampire with no blood effectively has no Self-Control against hunger stimuli.

Difficulty (Traits)Stimulus
OneSmell of blood when hungry
TwoSight of blood when hungry; harassment; a life-threatening situation
ThreePhysical provocation or attack; taste of blood when hungry
FourA loved one in danger; humiliation
FiveOutright humiliation; mortal insults

Remember: a character does not automatically frenzy merely from running out of blood, but with no Self-Control/Instinct Traits available to win a tie, she is very likely to frenzy the moment a qualifying stimulus appears. A failed Self-Control/Instinct test grants the permanent Negative Social Trait Callous or Condescending (player's choice), which can later be bought off normally.

Courage Difficulties (Rötschreck)

Mirrors the Self-Control table above, but for fire, sunlight, and other terror stimuli, resisted with Courage instead.

Difficulty (Traits)Stimulus
OneBeing bullied; a lighter; sunrise
TwoA torch; sunlight obscured by clouds or curtains
ThreeA bonfire; an uncovered window in daylight
FourA house fire; being burned
FiveTrapped in a burning building; direct sunlight

Golconda

A mystical state in which a vampire fully accepts the terms of the Curse. The Camarilla dismisses it as a fool's dream; the Sabbat and independents consider it beneath notice. The only firm mechanical rule: a character must maintain Humanity 4+ and Conscience 4+ to remain on a Golconda quest, or mentors abandon her until she atones. Golconda is a goal worth years of game time across multiple chronicles, not a quick unlock.

Benefits of achieved Golconda: spend only one Blood Trait per week (not per night) for sustenance; immunity to frenzy and Rötschreck (and to supernatural powers that would force either state); ability to learn all Disciplines regardless of clan or generation restriction. All benefits vanish immediately if the character falls from Golconda.
